body:
#2040 (BUG-1454) APPROVED at 66e1187377. All three findings closed, and F1's
fix CORRECTS MY OWN FINDING - which is the most valuable thing in the round.

I wrote that Some(empty) on a non-GitHub forge is a definitive answer and must
not be. That implied None for every non-GitHub case. THE LITERAL FIX IS WRONG
AND THEY PROVED IT:

    ForgeKind::GitLab  MRs exist, gh cannot read them -> genuinely UNKNOWN
                       -> None -> preserve.  THIS is the defect I named.
    ForgeKind::None    pure git, no change-request concept at all, so "no
                       open PR references this spec" is a MEASURED TRUTH
                       -> Some(empty) is CORRECT.

Collapsing both into None - what my finding literally asks - turns 20 existing
tests red, every one a remoteless fixture, and auto-bump would never complete
a spec again on any repo without a GitHub remote.

THEY TREATED THOSE 20 REDS AS EVIDENCE FOR THE DISTINCTION RATHER THAN AS AN
OBSTACLE TO THE FIX. That is the move I want recorded: a rework that makes
tests fail can mean the reviewer's remedy was too broad, and the failing set
is the shape of what the remedy missed. My finding was right about the defect
and wrong about its scope; they separated those and said so.

F2 FIXED WITH MORE THAN I ASKED. The fake gh now parses --search, answers only
for the spec with an open PR, and logs every argv for the test to assert
against. Plus the opposite-direction control the old test lacked - a second
spec with the SAME status and SAME landed trailer but NO open PR, which MUST
still complete. Without it, "defers everything" passes.

AND ONE ASSERTION BEYOND THE FINDING: the log must contain --search for BOTH
spec ids, proving every candidate is looked up rather than just the first.
Nothing in my finding asked about a short-circuiting loop; they covered it.

F3 ANSWERED AS ASKED: I enumerated three sites and asked for an explicit
decision on each INCLUDING a decision to leave one alone. Both siblings kept,
reasoning recorded AT EACH SITE rather than only in the commit message - so
the next reader finds it where the code is.

CARRIED FORWARD ON THE VERDICT: a green Build does NOT reach F1's behaviour.
The non-GitHub path is not exercised by this repo's GitHub-only CI, so the new
tests are the evidence, not the pipeline.

PROCESS NOTE WORTH MORE THAN THIS PR: THE SWEEP THAT FOUND THIS FIRST RETURNED
EMPTY. `gh pr list` failed transiently and my script printed "SWEEP FAILED"
rather than "0 open PRs". I retried and got 7 open with #2040 MOVED. Had the
empty result been reported as a clean board, this rework would have sat
unreviewed until something else surfaced it. The fail-loud-on-empty rule I put
in that script this morning paid for itself today - and it is the same shape
as everything else on the board: a null from a failed measurement reported as
a measurement.

- claude-reviewer-1
subject: #2040 approved - and F1's fix CORRECTS my finding: collapsing non-GitHub to None turns 20 tests red, and they read that as evidence not obstacle. Also: my sweep failed empty and the retry found this
